# Flags and environment

Every ceiling agentfs runs under is one row of a single table. A setting absent from that table cannot be set from the command line and cannot appear here, so this page is the whole surface.

Every flag has an environment variable: `AGENTFS_` followed by the flag name in upper case with dashes as underscores. The environment is applied first and flags second, so an explicit flag beats an exported variable — the more specific statement of intent is the later one. A variable whose value does not parse is ignored rather than fatal: an exported value is ambient, and refusing to start would let an unrelated shell setting break the tool.

`--format` selects the output form and is not part of the table; the values each command renders are in [cli.md](cli.md).

Settings are checked before a command runs, and every finding is reported from one pass, so a configuration is corrected whole rather than one start at a time. A value the program cannot run under exits `usage` naming the field, the flag, what the value must satisfy, and what it was.

## Relations

Two pairs have to hold together, beyond each setting's own floor:

- `-max-extra-bytes` must not exceed `-max-document-bytes`: preserved undefined members cannot outsize the document holding them.
- `-root-retry-min` must not exceed `-root-retry-max`: a backoff cannot start above its own ceiling.

## Workspace

The directory agentfs reads. It is set by the positional argument every command that reads a workspace requires, and there is no flag for it: one setting with two spellings would let a command line disagree with itself. Every path in a result is relative to it.

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | `AGENTFS_ROOT` | `path` | `.` | every command | Root is the directory agentfs observes; every path it reports is relative to it, and the root is opened confined so that no traversal, including one through a symlink, leaves the tree. |

## Selections

One spelling from a closed set. A spelling outside the set exits `usage` and names the permitted values.

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-watch` | `AGENTFS_WATCH` | `enum` | `auto` | every command | Watch selects change detection, with auto resolving to kernel notification on a local filesystem and to notification plus sweep on every other kind, because a write by another client of a network export raises no event on this host. |
| `-color` | `AGENTFS_COLOR` | `enum` | `auto` | `watch` | Color selects styling: auto styles only when the output is an interactive terminal, always styles whatever the output is, and never emits no escape sequence at all. |

`-watch` accepts `auto`, `notify`, `sweep`, `hybrid`.

`-color` accepts `auto`, `always`, `never`.

## Counts

How many things agentfs reads, holds or registers. Each one turns a quantity the workspace chooses — entries in a directory, events in a burst, nodes in a tree — into a number agentfs states, which is what makes bounded work something a test can assert. Crossing a count truncates the work and raises a diagnostic; see [diagnostics.md](diagnostics.md).

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-max-depth` | `AGENTFS_MAX_DEPTH` | `count` | `32` | every command | MaxDepth bounds descent below the root; the default is deeper than a real workspace layout and shallow enough that a pathological tree truncates with a diagnostic instead of walking without end. |
| `-max-entries-per-dir` | `AGENTFS_MAX_ENTRIES_PER_DIR` | `count` | `5000` | every command | MaxEntriesPerDir bounds the entries read from one directory; the default is larger than any directory a person lays out by hand, so a run directory an agent fills without bound costs one bounded listing and a truncation diagnostic rather than stalling the walk. |
| `-max-nodes` | `AGENTFS_MAX_NODES` | `count` | `200000` | every command | MaxNodes bounds the tree the model holds; the default spans a large checkout while keeping the node table proportional to a number agentfs chose rather than to whatever the workspace contains. |
| `-max-watches` | `AGENTFS_MAX_WATCHES` | `count` | `8192` | `watch` | MaxWatches bounds directory watch registrations, keeping agentfs inside a conservative per-user kernel watch budget and handing the remainder of a large tree to the sweep. |
| `-max-batch` | `AGENTFS_MAX_BATCH` | `count` | `4096` | `watch` | MaxBatch bounds the events folded into one model update; the default is half of MaxQueue, so a queue that has filled drains in two frames and a burst larger than that is reconciled by the sweep rather than applied in one long frame. |
| `-max-queue` | `AGENTFS_MAX_QUEUE` | `count` | `8192` | `watch` | MaxQueue bounds the events waiting to be applied; the default is two full batches, which is the backlog a burst may build without a frame missing its deadline, and a queue that fills degrades to a sweep reconciliation instead of growing until the process is killed. |
| `-max-feed-entries` | `AGENTFS_MAX_FEED_ENTRIES` | `count` | `2000` | `watch` | MaxFeedEntries bounds the activity feed, which is a ring: the default holds enough history to explain what an agent has been doing at a cost that does not grow with how long agentfs has been running. |
| `-max-diagnostics` | `AGENTFS_MAX_DIAGNOSTICS` | `count` | `500` | `watch` | MaxDiagnostics bounds retained findings; the default holds more distinct findings than a workspace has distinct ways of being wrong, and the overflow is counted and reported once, because a workspace that is wrong in one way is wrong in that way thousands of times. |
| `-sweep-budget` | `AGENTFS_SWEEP_BUDGET` | `count` | `512` | every command | SweepBudget bounds the directories one sweep pass reads; the default is the number a pass can read well inside SweepInterval, which is what keeps a sweep off the critical path of a frame however large the tree is. |

## Byte ceilings

How much agentfs reads from, or retains about, the workspace. A value is written as a plain byte count; the defaults below are rendered with a binary suffix.

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-max-preview-bytes` | `AGENTFS_MAX_PREVIEW_BYTES` | `bytes` | `1MiB` | `watch` | MaxPreviewBytes bounds the window a preview holds of any one file; a preview is a window onto a file rather than a copy of it, so the default is a fraction of the transcript an agent writes and a file whose size the workspace chose costs the window instead of the file. |
| `-max-document-bytes` | `AGENTFS_MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` | `bytes` | `1MiB` | every command | MaxDocumentBytes bounds a state document; a status declaration larger than the default is a log, and decoding it as state would spend the whole memory budget on one file. |
| `-max-extra-bytes` | `AGENTFS_MAX_EXTRA_BYTES` | `bytes` | `64KiB` | every command | MaxExtraBytes bounds the undefined members preserved per document; the default is the ceiling the state contract itself applies, so a document read by agentfs and one read by any conforming reader keep the same bytes, and reading a document written to a schema this build does not know cannot be turned into unbounded retention. |

## Time windows

How long agentfs waits, and how much clock difference it tolerates. A value is a Go duration such as `2s`, `500ms` or `1m30s`.

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-sweep-interval` | `AGENTFS_SWEEP_INTERVAL` | `duration` | `2s` | every command | SweepInterval is the period between sweep passes; the default is shorter than an operator's patience for stale output and long enough that a budgeted pass costs a fraction of one core. |
| `-dedup-ttl` | `AGENTFS_DEDUP_TTL` | `duration` | `2s` | `watch` | DedupTTL is the window within which repeated events for one path collapse to a single update, sized so that an editor's write-then-rename sequence lands inside it, and disabled at zero. |
| `-skew-tolerance` | `AGENTFS_SKEW_TOLERANCE` | `duration` | `5s` | every command | SkewTolerance is how far ahead of this host's clock a workspace timestamp may sit before it is reported as being from the future; the default is the tolerance the state contract names, wide enough for the drift between hosts sharing a mount and narrow enough that a genuinely wrong clock is still reported. |
| `-stale-after` | `AGENTFS_STALE_AFTER` | `duration` | `1m30s` | every command | StaleAfter is the silence after which a workspace is marked stale, longer than the pause between an agent's steps and shorter than the time an operator would spend trusting a dead pane. |
| `-root-retry-min` | `AGENTFS_ROOT_RETRY_MIN` | `duration` | `1s` | `watch` | RootRetryMin is the first delay before reopening a lost root, short enough that a brief unmount recovers before an operator reaches for the keyboard. |
| `-root-retry-max` | `AGENTFS_ROOT_RETRY_MAX` | `duration` | `30s` | `watch` | RootRetryMax is the ceiling the reopen backoff climbs to, bounding what agentfs spends on a root that does not come back while keeping the retry frequent enough to notice one that does. |

## Switches

A boolean. `-strict` sets it and `-strict=false` clears it.

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-strict` | `AGENTFS_STRICT` | `bool` | `false` | every command | Strict promotes every warning diagnostic to an error, so a workspace that reads with warnings fails a conformance run instead of passing it quietly, and reports a well-formedness error on the first reading rather than withholding it until a second reading agrees. |
| `-ascii` | `AGENTFS_ASCII` | `bool` | `false` | `watch` | ASCII restricts the frame to ASCII glyphs, for terminals and fonts that render box drawing and braille as replacement boxes. |

## Name lists

A comma-separated list of member names, in the same form on the command line and in the environment. An entry is neither blank nor contains a comma, and an empty value clears the list.

| Flag | Environment variable | Unit | Default | Read by | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-redact-keys` | `AGENTFS_REDACT_KEYS` | `list` | `api_key,apikey,authorization,cookie,credential,password,secret,token` | `watch` | RedactKeys names the document members whose values are masked before rendering, so a credential an agent writes into its own state is not put on a shared screen by the tool watching it. |
